correctness.rationale: Fourier lower bound for the sum of cyclic Gram correlations is globally valid for arbitrary unit vectors, including asymmetric/rank-unbounded feasible SDP solutions. Explicit three-dimensional Fourier vectors attain the exact scalar minimum. Cut enumeration by negative-leaf count gives the integer optimum. Exact quadratic gaps, discriminants and strict algebraic ratio-endpoint comparison prove all n>=3,t>=0 statements. Finite exact-rational and random checks corroborate, not substitute for the derivation.

originality.rationale: Topic-specific searches of published mathematical findings and available predecessor claims returned no logically covering weighted-wheel SDP claim. Read general SDP and Grothendieck theory plus the 2016 paper with numeric t=1 wheel cases. Neither the general framework nor the finite t=1 table entails the all-real-t exactness classification and unique 7-to-9 worst-gap switch. The 1993 Delorme--Poljak paper is an explicitly documented full-text access risk, so this is a qualified self-review originality assessment, not a proof of global literature novelty.

Non-indexed or differently named analytic solutions could exist; search and proof comparison do not certify absolute novelty.
The 2016 numerical unweighted-wheel SDP values are known and not claimed as new; all-t formulas and switch are the distinctive claim.

value.rationale: The canonical GW relaxation is a meaningful benchmark. Exact support-function and integer optima for a continuous weighted wheel family identify precise SDP exactness and a genuinely structural, sharp 7-to-9 odd-wheel transition in the maximizer of the integrality gap; not a single unmotivated graph computation. The isolated n=3 exactness point provides a useful boundary case. The scope excludes arbitrary spoke-weight vectors and strengthened relaxations.
